samples.summary: The runHunt wiring for scopedTitle/overclaimed (and the stats.overclaimed counter) has no test — every test uses a CONFIRMED fixture that carries neither field
samples.evidence: hunt-ui.mjs:1357-1359 adds `record.scopedTitle = uiScopedTitle(...)`, `record.overclaimed = uiOverclaimed(...)` and `if (record.overclaimed) stats.overclaimed++`. The funnel fixture `CONFIRMED` (hunt-ui.test.mjs:861-868) contains no `scopedTitle` and no `overclaimed`, so the end-to-end tests (`runHunt carries a real candidate all the way to a report`, line 910) only ever exercise the fallback path. No test anywhere asserts `out.stats.overclaimed` (grep for `stats.` in hunt-ui.test.mjs shows proposed/unique/novel/reproduced/reported/refutedAfterReplay/cappedUnverified/unjudgedVerifier/actionsRun only), nor that `out.reported[0].scopedTitle` equals the verifier's value. If the assignment were dropped, mis-ordered (e.g. placed after `reported.push`), or the counter incremented in the wrong branch, every test still passes. The unit tests for uiScopedTitle/uiOverclaimed cover the helpers but not their integration, which is where the counter lives.

samples.summary: The ~30 new lines of verifier prompt instructing `scopedTitle`/`overclaimed` are untested, though the file has an established precedent for pinning prompt content
samples.evidence: verifyUi's prompt gains a whole '## And then bound the CLAIM to the evidence' section (hunt-ui.mjs:509-535). The existing test 'the verifier is told the scope and the path format it is the sole source of' (hunt-ui.test.mjs:260-286) captures `seenPrompt` and asserts on its content precisely because an instruction silently missing from the prompt is invisible. No equivalent assertion exists for the new section — the prompt could stop asking for a scopedTitle entirely and the suite stays green, while the schema-required field would then be filled arbitrarily by the model.

samples.summary: 'overclaiming does NOT block the gate' asserts a property no code in this diff implements — it passes identically before and after the change
samples.evidence: The test builds a verdict `{...CONFIRMED, overclaimed: true, scopedTitle: 'narrower'}` and asserts `isFilingVerdict(...) === true`. `isFilingVerdict` lives in hunt-gate.mjs and was not changed to read either field; the adjacent test at line 369 already asserts `true` for the same record/persona with a verdict lacking those fields. So the assertion holds regardless of the new behavior — it is a future-regression guard, not coverage of anything this diff adds, yet it is presented under a heading implying the gate was exercised against overclaiming.
searchedFor: grep overclaimed in hunt-gate.mjs (only schema properties/required)

samples.summary: renderUiReport's fallback heading (`c.scopedTitle ?? k.title`) when no scopedTitle is present is not covered by any test
samples.evidence: Both new render tests (hunt-ui.test.mjs:335 and :355) supply a `scopedTitle` on the reported record. No test renders a record with `scopedTitle` undefined or `""` to pin that the hunter title is headlined and that no 'narrowed by the verifiers' note appears — which is exactly the branch where the `??` at line 774 and the truthiness check at line 781 disagree (an empty-string scopedTitle would render `### [major] ` with no title, and no test would notice).
searchedFor: grep renderUiReport call sites in hunt-ui.test.mjs

samples.summary: The new cmdRun stderr summary line for `stats.overclaimed` has no test, including its suppression when the count is zero
samples.evidence: hunt-ui.mjs:1061-1066 conditionally appends `${stats.overclaimed} reported finding(s) the verifiers had to narrow`. No test in hunt-ui.test.mjs invokes cmdRun or asserts on this output string (grep for 'had to narrow' / 'cmdRun' finds nothing), so both the wording and the zero-suppression are unverified.

samples.summary: uiScopedTitle is not tested for verifier disagreement — two verifiers supplying different scoped titles
samples.evidence: The test passes `[scoped, scoped]` (identical objects) and `[{scopedTitle:'  '}, scoped]`. It never asserts what happens when two verifiers supply genuinely different scoped titles, which is the documented 'first non-empty wins' policy and the one behavior where a silent choice is made among conflicting model prose. As written, the first assertion would pass even if the implementation joined, sorted, or picked the last element.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. runHunt is only exercised from scripts/agent/hunt-ui.test.mjs (grep for `runHunt` matched no other file besides the .trusted baseline copies). Every runHunt test builds on funnelDeps (hunt-ui.test.mjs:883-908) whose verifyImpl returns CONFIRMED (:861-868), a six-field object with neither `scopedTitle` nor `overclaimed`; the per-test verifyImpl overrides (:1013, :1021, :1035, :1063, :1109, :1154) only set verdict:"refuted" or throw. A repo-wide grep for scopedTitle|overclaimed in the test file returns only helper unit tests (:290-318), an isFilingVerdict gate test (:331), and renderUiReport tests fed hand-built reported[] literals (:344, :362) — never a runHunt output. No assertion anywhere on out.reported[0].scopedTitle, out.reported[0].overclaimed, or out.stats.overclaimed; the renderer's stats line (hunt-ui.mjs:1064-1065) is likewise untested (grep "reported finding|verifiers had to" matches only the source). So the wiring at hunt-ui.mjs:1356-1361 — including the stats.overclaimed increment initialized at :1128 — could be deleted, reordered after reported.push, or incremented in the wrong branch with every test still green. This is a new behavior (the .trusted baseline test file contains no occurrence of either field) shipped with no meaningful integration test, which is a major "missing tests" finding under this lens. No counterexample found in scripts/agent, eval/, hunt-gate.mjs, or the trusted baseline.
